Subject: Request: regional fallback + uptime appendix and order-form language

Hi Olivia / Medilinx procurement team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — quick follow-up from our side as you start legal/procurement review. Medilinx's use case (multi-region failover for critical eCRF processing) makes a couple of tailored items important on our end:

1) Regional fallback policy: Medilinx wants a formal appendix that documents how Redwood will handle cross-region failover for traffic when primary region capacity is impacted. Specifically they want:
   - an explicit description of the automated fallback behavior, including max expected additional latency (P95) and a short list of regions we may route to for resilience;
   - a mechanism for pre-authorized temporary regional failovers for planned maintenance windows.

2) Tiered uptime/latency credit schedule: instead of a single uptime SLA, Medilinx is requesting tiered credits keyed to availability buckets (e.g., <99.9%, 99.7-99.9%, <99.7%) and a companion latency target for P95 during business hours.

3) Evidence & operational playbook: they'll need an exhibit that describes evidence types (incident timeline, per-route latency charts, token-level traces) and who to contact for operational escalations.

I attached a short diagram of the proposed fallback flow and an initial draft order-form language. Can your procurement/legal team review and let us know which items need firmed-up language vs. negotiation? If helpful we can produce a redline MSA exhibit.

Attachments: regional-fallback-diagram.png, redwood-orderform-draft.docx

Proposed next steps: if we can align on high-level structure this week, Soojin (legal) will slot precise exhibit language and Laura will update the order form for signature. Could you confirm a target for final review — are you planning to take this to internal legal next week?

Thanks,
Marcus

Subject: Re: Request: regional fallback + uptime appendix and order-form language

Hi Olivia — looping in legal on the thread. Quick thoughts and proposed language snippets below.

On credits: Redwood can accept a tiered model, but to keep order form simplicity we propose a 2-tier practical implementation:
  - Availability >= 99.95%: no credit;
  - Availability < 99.95% and >= 99.7%: 5% monthly service credit;
  - Availability < 99.7%: 15% monthly service credit.

Note: the above is intentionally asymmetric to reflect typical production economics. If Medilinx prefers exactly two visible buckets we can collapse to >=99.9% / <99.9% — discuss below.

On latency targets: for primary-region routing we propose P95 <= 120ms (in-region, business hours). For automated cross-region fallback we will commit to P95 <= 420ms as an upper bound during fallback events, with a notice describing expected uplift.

Proposed exhibit excerpt (draft language):
"Regional Fallback Exhibit: Redwood will implement automated regional fallback in accordance with the Regional Fallback Diagram (Exhibit A). During fallback, Redwood will route traffic to the next-available region on the customer's account. Customer understands that cross-region routing may increase per-request latency; Redwood's committed P95 latency during automated failover is <= 420ms. Redwood will provide incident timelines and per-route telemetry as evidence in the form of exported traces and latency histograms for the relevant time window."

We also suggest adding a short "pre-authorized maintenance" clause allowing Medilinx to pre-approve scheduled cross-region maintenance windows no less than 48 hours in advance so we can surface expected uplift and avoid credits for planned maintenance.

I'll draft a formal redline for the MSA exhibit and a matching order-form clause this afternoon.

Soojin Lee

Thanks Soojin & Laura — Medilinx legal and cloud ops reviewed the proposed exhibit. High level: we can accept the fallback approach and the pre-authorized maintenance box, but legal wants two small edits:

1) Replace the flat 420ms P95 fallback commitment with a "not to exceed" phrasing tied to distance — they want wording like: "Redwood's committed P95 latency during automated failover will not exceed 420ms unless routing to a region >X ms RTT as documented in Exhibit A." They will supply a short table of region pairs and RTT estimates.

2) Evidence retention: legal requests that exported traces used as evidence be retained for a minimum of 90 days.

Procurement: please provide a final redline and we can route for signature. Also send a DocuSign envelope when ready (we prefer electronic signature).

Olivia
